Q: How can the default Node.js version be set using NVM? A:

This will set the default to be the most current version of Node.js:

nvm alias default node

And then you'll need to run

nvm use default

Or exit and open a new tab.

Q: Java Apple KeyStore or SSL TrustManager which trusts certificates from both admin and root keychains A:

You can run java -XshowSettings:security -version to see what your JDK supports

On my system (java --version says openjdk version "21.0.9" 2025-10-21) ONLY KeychainStore is supported

[...]
----------------------------------------
Provider name: Apple
Provider information: Apple Provider
Provider services: (type : algorithm)
KeyStore.KeychainStore
----------------------------------------
[...]

Therefore this small test-program (ListDefaultTrustedCertificates.java)

import javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory;
import javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager;
import java.security.KeyStore;
import java.security.cert.X509Certificate;

public class ListDefaultTrustedCertificates {

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // This is what JSSE does internally
        TrustManagerFactory tmf =
                TrustManagerFactory.getInstance(
                        TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm());

        // null = use default truststore (system properties, OS store, etc.)
        tmf.init((KeyStore) null);

        X509TrustManager tm =
                (X509TrustManager) tmf.getTrustManagers()[0];

        X509Certificate[] certs = tm.getAcceptedIssuers();

        System.out.println("Trusted certificates count: " + certs.length);
        System.out.println();

        for (X509Certificate c : certs) {
            System.out.println(" Subject : " + c.getSubjectX500Principal());
            System.out.println(" Issuer  : " + c.getIssuerX500Principal());
            System.out.println();
        }
    }
}

called with

  -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStoreType=KeychainStore-Root \
  -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStoreProvider=Apple \
  ListDefaultTrustedCertificates.java

brought the stack exception (as expected):

    at java.base/sun.security.ssl.TrustStoreManager.getTrustedCerts(TrustStoreManager.java:57)

Q: Open an existing spreadsheet in write_only mode A:

No, this isn’t possible in openpyxl, and it’s not just a missing feature.

write_only=True is a streaming mode that’s meant for creating a brand-new workbook while keeping memory usage low. It never builds the normal in-memory representation of worksheets and cells. An existing Excel template, on the other hand, requires reading and preserving sheet XML, styles, shared strings, relationships, etc. Those two goals conflict.

In practice, openpyxl always writes a new .xlsx file on save anyway. To support “opening an existing workbook in write-only mode”, it would still have to load enough global state from the template to reproduce it correctly, which largely defeats the purpose of write-only streaming.

That’s why the usual low-memory approach is the one Charlie Clark outlined in the comments: open the template with read_only=True, create a separate Workbook(write_only=True), stream or recreate the sheets you need (often using named styles), and then append the large datasets. You’re effectively rewriting the workbook, but without holding everything in memory.

There are a few hard limitations to be aware of: worksheets can’t be copied between workbooks in openpyxl, and copy_worksheet() doesn’t work in read-only or write-only mode. If you need per-cell formatting from the template, you have to recreate it explicitly (named styles help, but there’s no zero-copy solution).

So the short answer is that openpyxl can’t add a write-only sheet to an existing workbook without breaking the streaming model, and the read-only -> write-only pipeline is the intended way to handle large outputs.

Q: Filling Missing Nodes with two-way grouping preferably in XSLT 1.0? A:

As noted in comments insertion of missing attriutes and node() text broke normalisation slightly. My modified XSL:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
Source - https://stackoverflow.com/a/79860293
Posted by Zeeshan Ahmad
Retrieved 2026-01-04, License - CC BY-SA 4.0
-->
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0"
xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">

<xsl:output method="xml" indent="yes"/>
<xsl:strip-space elements="*"/>

<!-- Identity transform -->
<xsl:template match="node()">
<xsl:copy>
<xsl:apply-templates select="@*|node()"/>
</xsl:copy>
</xsl:template>

<!-- Section-level processing -->
<xsl:template match="Section">
<xsl:copy>
<xsl:copy-of select="node()"/>

<!-- Cache column stencil -->
<xsl:variable name="columns"
select="Segment[Entry[@desgn='Columns']][1]/Entry[@desgn='Columns']"/>

<!-- Process each Segment -->
<xsl:for-each select="Segment">
<xsl:choose>
<!-- RowVals segment: normalize to full grid -->
<xsl:when test="Entry[@desgn='RowVals']">
<xsl:variable name="rvy"><xsl:value-of select="Entry[@desgn='RowVals']/@y"/></xsl:variable>
<Segment>
<xsl:for-each select="$columns">
<xsl:variable name="col" select="."/>
<xsl:variable name="cell"
select="../..//Segment[Entry[@desgn='RowVals']]
/Entry[@desgn='RowVals' and @ref=$col/@ref]
[../@y=current()/../@y]"/>
<xsl:choose>
<xsl:when test="$cell">
<xsl:copy-of select="$cell">
</xsl:copy-of>
</xsl:when>
<xsl:otherwise>
<Entry>
<xsl:copy-of select="$col/@z"/>
<xsl:attribute name="y">
<xsl:value-of select="$rvy"/>
</xsl:attribute>
<xsl:copy-of select="$col/@x"/>
<xsl:attribute name="desgn">RowVals</xsl:attribute>
<xsl:copy-of select="$col/@ref"/>
</Entry>
</xsl:otherwise>
</xsl:choose>

</xsl:for-each>
</Segment>
</xsl:when>

<!-- Non-RowVals segments pass through unchanged -->
<xsl:otherwise>
<xsl:copy-of select="."/>
</xsl:otherwise>

</xsl:choose>
</xsl:for-each>
</xsl:copy>
</xsl:template>

</xsl:stylesheet>

With the consequent sample breakage:
<TabularDoc>

<Segment>
<Entry z="12.55" y="1.4" x="1.1" desgn="Table" ref="VDevelopment">Verifying Development</Entry>
</Segment>
<Segment>

<Entry z="12.55" y="2.4" x="2.3" desgn="Columns" ref="Selection">Selection</Entry>

</Segment>

</Segment>
<Segment>

</Segment>

</Segment>

<Entry z="12.55" y="2.4" x="2.3" desgn="Columns" ref="Selection">Selection</Entry>
<Entry z="12.55" y="2.4" x="3.3" desgn="Columns" ref="Choice">Choice</Entry>
</Segment>

<Entry z="12.55" y="3.4" x="1.3" desgn="RowVals" ref="WIndex"/>

My main sin was to change @* into node() to expose missing text() at the top <Section> tree fragment

Q: Conflicting acronym capitalization in core method names A:

The Google JavaScript style guide lists newCustomerId as correct and newCustomerID as incorrect.

Also see duplicate questions: ID, id, or Id and ID or Id on User Interface

Nothing has changed since these were asked decades ago.

Q: Restrict access by roles in Symfony A:

To restrict access to a specific method in Symfony, I think the easiest way is to add a security tag (either an Annotation or an Attribute) directly above your function.

Please take a look at: https://symfony.com/doc/current/security/expressions.html
